title: Vanishing on the closed fibre over a valuation ring descends to some A/pi
statement: Let A be a valuation ring with maximal ideal \mathfrak m, assume A is not a field, let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let X_0 be the closed fibre, let L be an invertible module on X [def-sc-invertible-module], and let s\in\Gamma(X,L) with s|_{X_0}=0. Then there is a nonzero \pi\in\mathfrak m such that s restricts to zero on X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(A/\pi).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, proof sentence 'kappa = colim A/pi ... see Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-section'

proof.text: Since A is not a field, its maximal ideal m contains a nonzero element. Order the nonzero elements of m by divisibility. Because A is a valuation ring, this is a directed index system, A/m is the filtered colimit of the quotients A/pi, and Spec(A/m) is the inverse limit of the affine schemes Spec(A/pi). Base change of the finitely presented morphism f along these affine maps gives an inverse system X x_Spec(A) Spec(A/pi) with affine transition maps and limit X_0. Choose one nonzero pi_0 in m and set F_{pi_0}=L|_{X x_Spec(A) Spec(A/pi_0)}; its pullbacks to later stages and to X_0 are the corresponding restrictions of L, and s restricts to a compatible system of sections.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0EX8 proof, paragraph beginning 'Then kappa = A/m = colim A/pi'

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-valuation-limit-qcoh-section-descent] to F_{pi_0} and the section s|_{X x_Spec(A) Spec(A/pi_0)}. Since the pullback of this section to X_0 is s|_{X_0}=0, the eventual-zero clause gives a later stage indexed by a nonzero pi in m for which the restriction of s to X x_Spec(A) Spec(A/pi) is zero, as required.
